body: In March 2024, I told my readers about our ascent of Sri Lanka’s Adam Peak (aka Śrī Pāda or Adam’s Peak), which is in a mountainous area in Sabaragamuwa province. And I ended my post by saying that there are TWO Adam Peaks on the Island. The second is Little Adam's Peak (1,151 meters high), located near the town of Ella in Uva Province. Even then I read that climbing the "Little Adam" is even more interesting, as climbing is much easier, and the views from its summit are particularly interesting and colorful. And here I am, all so magical after EXACTLY ONE YEAR, fulfilled the dream of personal travel tablets – I am back in Ceylon, and I did climb Little Adam’s Peak!!! Although there are only 124 kilometres between Adam Peak and Adam Lesser Peak, the difference is stark: in the first you storm the MOUNTAIN, in the second you climb the HILL cheerfully. Although it must be acknowledged that Little Adam is a mountain that is part of the Badulla County mountain system. Where Little Adam's Peak came from - I never understood. There are several versions: one says it's after the "big brother" that the uniform resembles. Some argue that it is an Aboriginal marketing move to add to the attraction of the facility. Can the knowledgeable tell? From where we were stationed in Ella - apartments at the Meditation monastery Sri Sumanarama temple that's on Temple Road, Google maps gave four versts to the summit and a minimum of an hour of footdrilling. Since most of the route ran first through the city, and then along the hiking trail, they decided not to take a tuk-tuk to the foot and just stretch their legs. So after an early breakfast, they immediately moved on. The night mist and haze had just begun to clear, allowing for quite decent photos. The climb isn't really hard - there's no comparison to Adam's Peak. Therefore, it is even suitable for people far from mountaineering (as the author of these lines). On the way, and from the viewing platform itself, super atmospheric videos open up - I photographed tirelessly, afraid of missing all the interesting things. Revisiting the footage afterwards, he found that he had managed to photograph almost everything three or four times, but in that “moment of happiness” each frame was perceived as something new and interesting. On their way back they went through tea plantations that stretch on the slopes near the trail - a sight unusual and thus very interesting. A visit to Little Adam’s Peak is one of the most memorable events of our Sri Lankan trip. I recommend it!!!
title: Our second Sri Lankan summit in honour of the “forefather of mankind”

body: Aug 2025 • FamilyNeutral review. Visited Aug 22nd and just about to start the climb up when there was an exodus of people descending to escape a bee swarm attack. Two women carried down fireman style by staff who literally ran down the steps. Kudos to staff, they appeared to be doing a good job evacuating, especially the two chaps who carried wounded down. One women was very badly stung and taken away by ambulance. Another half dozen walking wounded taken by truck to hospital.Returned today after the rain and had a very quiet visit. Thunderstorm an hour before meant it was virtually deserted on top.Now the ‘could do better’. Apparently drones can set bees into swarm mode. No idea if this caused yesterday’s incident, but it is a risk. There is one sign prohibiting drones, but (a) it isn’t very prominent and doesn’t say why, and (b) there is no attempt at enforcement. I had sharp words with someone about to launch today, who had no idea of the risks (probably none today after the rain, but I wasn’t taking the chance) A few more (graphic) notices about why drones are banned would raise awareness.Positive: it’s a nice view. It’s not pristine wilderness: the zip line and swing and pool bar with thumping bass will not be to everyone’s liking. But I guess these things keep general access free and provide staff cover for incidents like yesterday. Worth a visit, but if allergic to bee stings I would not risk it (same story 9-arches bridge)
title: Beware of bee swarms

From 9 onwards you can zip line down, ride a swing, shoot air rifles and climb a wall all for an extra cost. The zip line is 9900.rupees for adults and 6000 for kids. There is a spectacular bar and pool area that looks amazing too. We paid a tuk tuk 3000 return trip and our calves/glutes thanked us

body: Little Adam's Peak is a popular hiking destination in Sri Lanka. Located in the Ella region, it offers stunning panoramic views of the surrounding countryside and tea plantations. The hike is relatively easy and accessible, making it suitable for a wide range of fitness levels. It gets its name from the larger Adam's Peak (Sri Pada) due to the resemblance in shape. The trail typically takes around 1 to 2 hours to complete, and the summit provides a great vantage point for photography and enjoying the natural beauty of Sri Lanka.
title: Little Adam's Peak is a popular hiking destination in Sri Lanka. Located in the Ella region, it offers stunning panoramic views

body: Nice ride. The entrance is on foot or by tuktuk to avoid a ten minute walk. Then the rather steep climb lasts 30-40 minutes, we did it with children of 3 years and 5 months in baby carrier. The view is beautiful.

body: Mixed feelings about this one….. I would say that it is definitely a case of “should have been here 5 years ago” - maps show a mix of trails to L A P but these have now been gated off to steer you strictly past the super tacky and out of place pool club, cafe, zip line and rock climbing wall absolutely ruining the natural feel of an outdoor walk to a view point. We were lucky in a way that we were just after sunrise so the Insta’s, sorry “content creators” were all on their way down as we were going up (roughly 6:30 am), we actually had the peak to ourselves (plus one coconut man) for a long while. The walk to the highest peak is easy enough (all stairs), but the walk to the next peak is a tricky scramble up and down with no stairs or rails, just slippery dirt and rocks. Views are nice from both peaks, depends whether you prefer a more distant view down to the coast (second peak) or a view featuring the second peak. As we were coming back, more people were arriving and there was quite a crowd heading up (these were mostly tour group type people). So despite missing the sunrise/ best light, we do feel like we got the best timing re having the peak to ourselves for so long.In summary a nice view and walk well on its way to being ruined. Shame on the operators/ developers
title: A nice walk steadily being ruined - shame

body: Little Adam's Peak was an experience that left me in awe of the breathtaking natural beauty. I ascended in solitude at 0500 to avoid the midday heat and crowds. The path wasn’t difficult to navigate since it was well marked and I could see it just fine as the first light came through. When I reached the top, I was rewarded with stunning panoramic views. It’s said to be a moderately difficult hike, but even with injured feet, I was able to ascend just fine. When I descended, I was able to see the surroundings of lush greenery, tea plantations, and rolling hills that I couldn’t really make out early in the morning. Little Adam's Peak is a gem of Sri Lanka's natural splendor. Highly recommend if you’re up for a moderate hike!
title: A gem

body: Eager to see what the "Little Adams peak" is like, I had to attempt the climb twice as in the first attempt somewhere halfway a sudden heavy downpour disrupted the journey. I had to hurriedly retreat to Flying Ravana ticketing centre for refuge. The thunderstorm lasted for about an hour and I gave up the idea of climbing and came to the pool club to spend the rest of the time. However, after the rain ceased the haze or the mist passed off and as there was some time to dusk, I decided to get back on the trail once again. This time I was well passed at least three quarters of the journey when the hell broke loose again drenching me severely. There was no shelter or a canopy for shade and the only option was to proceed until I reached the summit. Luckily for me there was no thunder or lightning. It was hazy at the beginning but with the ceasing of the rain it began to clear off, giving me good visibility of the surrounding mountain ranges and the distance water falls including the upper segment of "Ravana falls". My journey was well worth as the panoramic views were extremely beautiful. I had the best view of Ella gap and beyond. Up there I could not find any clue to why it is called little Adams peak, but there must be some legend behind it.
title: Trail that helped burn my calories

body: If you're looking for a fun and easy climbing adventure in Kandy, then Little Peaks Adam is definitely worth checking out. The climb takes about 30 minutes and is relatively easy, but you'll want to wear good sneakers to ensure a steady grip on the rocks. There are three tops to the climb, with the last one being a bit more challenging to reach, but the incredible views of the valley and mountains in front of you make it all worth it.One of the best things about Little Peaks Adam is its location. The main entrance to the climb is only a 15-minute walk from Kandy village, making it easy to access and a great way to spend an afternoon. And once you reach the top, you'll be rewarded with panoramic views that will take your breath away.Overall, I highly recommend Little Peaks Adam for anyone looking for a fun and rewarding outdoor adventure in Kandy. The climb is easy enough for most people to enjoy, but still challenging enough to make you feel accomplished when you reach the top. And the views are simply stunning, making it an unforgettable experience.
title: Scaling New Heights: Discovering the Breathtaking Views of Little Peaks Adam in Kandy

body: If you have done any decent hike or any trek with good views, this will be a disappointment. There is absolutely nothing special about the view from top. Infact when I reached the peak, I had to ask someone if this was it or was there anything more. The hike and views are basic. Ella infact as a town was the least attractive and offered nothing extraordinary. It is something one can skip.
title: Nothing extraordinary. Basic views and hike

body: Busy place but did not take too long for the food! Very cool and helpful staff! Thanks Rumesh for the service :-)
title: Nice staff

body: Short hike to the peak, lots of concrete/stone steps to make the walk up easier. Great views, we went in the morning and it's wasn't crowded. No entrance fee to go up to the Peak. There are optional paid activities at the peak, including zip line and absailing.
title: Great view with no entrance fee

body: Little Adam’s peak is more of a walk than a hike, which is great for a warm up or with children. From 98 acres, the walk up takes a little under 20 minutes. There is a stop at the zip line about 1/3 of the way thee with a bathroom. When you arrive at the top there is a main peak where you can get a coconut water. The main view is breathtaking, and on the other side is a small shrine that has equally great views.
title: Quick walk with amazing views

body: Easy walk, suitable for all. My pregnant wife managed it with relative ease. There are a few steep steps but taking them slowly is all the precaution needed.Once at the top you can walk part of the ridge line to other great views. Done slowly the walk up, a little time spent admiring the views, and back down again with the customary photos took us 2.5hrs
title: Easy walk. Enjoy it, don’t rush

body: Its quite an easy walk up the peak from the town and the view is lovely. Its also on the way to 9 arch bridge so you can do the whole lot in an afternoon!
title: Easy walk up

body: There is a beautiful trail that leads up to the Peak with 360c views over the valley and Ella Rock. It takes approximately 30 minutes to walk up at a steady speed. The hike is gentle and not challenging so it is well suited to all ages and fitness levels.
title: Kick-start your day!

body: Nice for Family with young children also. Is very close to the train bridge. The views are amazing and the hole area is very clean.
title: 45 min trip

body: We climbed little Adams peak for sunrise. The walk didn’t take too long; around 30 minutes in total to get to the top. The views were absolutely breathtaking of Ella rock and the valley below Ella.We would highly recommend this hike if you want to see the sunrise. The path up wasn’t always the most clear; if you keep to the left of the construction site, you should get to the tea plantation, and from there take the steps up to the very top
title: Recommend for an easy sunrise climb

body: What a great place. Easy to hike. Not as difficult as I expected it to be. Breath taking view was well worth the hike. Tends to fog a bit so make sure you go there at the right times. Was a great walk and something I would like to do again
title: Hikes

body: Really great and easy walk, perfect for morning or evening. If you are fit enough, don't plan it for the whole day. The view is beautiful and we were lucky to be almost alone on the top and enjoyed much. There is an option of some extreme riding there, you'll find their office on the way, but we didn't try that
title: Nice view and really easy

body: Hike is not difficult, takes about 30-45 mins from 98 Acres entrance. View is amazing at the top. We missed the sunset due to clouds.
title: Amazing view

body: Rather easy hike to the first two mountain tops; the 3rd is bit difficult; but we still made it with a 6 year old kid. Recommend to take the hike in early mornings; before the sun burns down. Once on the peaks, you will not be disappointed with the 360 degree vistas showing the beauty of Ella's mountains and lush greenary.
title: Best Views in Ella

body: We took our 5 year old daughter along with us and she had a blast... starts with a easy walk through a tea plantation, followed by a few flights of stairs that lead you to a few meters of rock terrain... before you know it your at the top in 20-25 mins... Take a bottle of water, sun glasses and a good camera and be prepared to spend about 30-45 mins at the top... the view is breathtaking and it’s best if you can stay on and soak it all in, as opposed to rushing back down... The “Flying Ravana” is just at the beginning of the hike and you might want to set aside 3-4 hours of your doing both of it (including the quad bikes that take 1 hour)...
title: Fantastic Experience!!!

body: A must do walk if you go to Ella. Have a small climb at the end to reach the peak which is nothing. Visitors will go through Flying Ravana adventure park so they will have more options to enjoy while exploring the peak.
title: Easy walk

body: It's super way to reach top relax place you can meet some tea factory and peoples around you good view for photo it's fantastic place to visit
title: Take care of your self and others

body: Lovely view from the top. There is quite a climb, not difficult but can be a challenge to someone not used to.Went there by tuk tuk
title: Lovely view

body: Not too difficult to get to the top but would recommend trainers or similar footwear, not flip flops. Some steep steps and clambering but well worth the effort. It took about 30/40 minutes from the entrance by the Flower Garden Resort. Spectacular 360’ views at the top.
title: Fabulous views

body: We stayed at flower garden resort, and lillte Adam's peak was a nice treck thru tea bushes and climb ..took 35 minutes gentle walk..best time to set foot is before 5.30am , reach top before 6am is the best..breathtaking view and the climb is not recommended for elders...you could see the sky changing colour as the Ray's if the sun appear from the rear of mountain peaks from east of srilanka...
title: A treck to little Adam's peak

body: Best view comes after the hardest climb.it was so pictures .chilled nice breeze unforgettable experience
title: Nice view

body: Best place to see the sunrise or sunset, also there are several other adventure activities at the premises.
title: Easy hike in Ella

body: It was about 2 hours hike up and down. We had to park on the road at the entrance to 98 acres hotel and walk from there. We went early in the morning around 6.30 am. Ideal time as weather is cooler and nice for photography.
title: Lovely hike and Stunning views

body: We can touch the clouds. That much we ate close to sky. Mountains are look a like Heaven... You can see Hambantota also
title: You Can Touch The Heaven

body: Very tiring climb. Makes you wonder if its worth it as there no place with shade to rest on top. Wonderful view for sure!! More than five hundreds steps to climb from the base where the hotel is.
title: Is it worth it?

body: It is an easy hiking track for an hour, 40meters stairs up at the end. Beautiful view from the top and worths to visit.
title: Nice view

body: One of the best hike which take around 1 hour to reach the top. The most important thing is the place is very easy to find and access.
title: best place to visit

body: While it is a tad strenuous on the way back, but it not as bad as people made it put to be. The trek to the view point is fairly short and you can take a break at an intermediate view point with the Buddha statue. The view there is nice but do make it to the end for even better views :)There is also a zipline place on the way up.
title: Worth the view at the End

body: Good sunset view, can be a bit busy but there is plenty of space to take photos. Takes about an hour to walk up and the path is well laid out. Free to visit.
title: Good sunset view

body: Was a little busy along the way, so be prepared to share the experience with many others. Take a good camera as lovely views to capture
title: Lovely easy walk

body: Had great time walking to the top of Adam’s Pick. Amazing view! It wasn’t difficult and enjoyed drinks that local were making on our way.
title: Amazing!

body: It's a scenic walk past villages. Then there is a steep climb up the mountain. But this is doable. The views once you are at the top are simply stunning. Rather go in the morning and wear a good pair of walking shoes.
title: Spectacular views

body: Very beautiful mountain, easy to climb up,you can watch amazing view from the top, some places are slippery need to be careful,if you are visiting to ella you must go to this place,There is a Zip line service and ATV Bike service available in this place,Zip line service was 20 Dollars per person,I think it is not valuable for the Price,it is around 500m Zip line, I've seen that ATV Bike service was 40 dollars per person but i didn't had time to try it,If you are going to this visit Little Adams peak from Ella town my suggestion is take little walk,if you are hire a Tuk Tuk they will charge around 700 rupees
title: Beautiful

body: It was a very nice view to see! It's worth the climb especially if you enjoy getting really nice pictures of nature!
title: Beautiful view!

body: The walk is challenging in the middle of the day, especially the last few hundred metres, which are relatively steep. But once up there, it's really beautiful. Just take some water (or you can get some at the top) and a snack, and take lots of pictures. Probably avoid the selfies right near the edge though, they make everyone anxious..
title: Stunning views

body: This is one of the must-do activities when visiting Ella. We were lucky that we booked and stayed at “Chillout Ella” Hotel where is located right at the entry point of the hiking. Hiking is relatively easy for anyone at all ages with good fitness level since most of the paths are not so steep and built with staircase. Generally, it took us about 45 mins or less to climb up to the top where it provides stunning panoramic views of the mountain ranges. There is no fee required to enter this hiking trail and zip line activities is available along the way for those who seek more adventurous fun! This activities can be combined with visiting to Nine Arch Bridge as there is a connecting path going to Nine Arch Bridge. A good 3 hours to be spent here or longer especially for nature trekking lovers!
title: Beautiful Panoramic views!!!

body: This peak was within walking distance of our hotel (“98 Acres”). Well marked route with gravel path and steps, some parts in shade but gets very hot so take plenty of water. When we went there was someone selling cold drinks at the top! Great views when you get there. Part way up there is a zip wire base station - two 550 metre lines across the valley, looked awesome, very well organised and safety standards seemed very good though we didn’t try it! Tip: Go early in the morning for less crowded, less hot experience.
title: Hard climb but Great views, can be crowded

body: I climbed this on my own as my husband is blind so he waited with our guide at the bottom. the climb is good, lots of steps and only 2 parts that are rocks and uneven.The zip wire looked fun but not very long. Views from the top were great.
title: glad I did this

body: We decided not to walk up for the sunrise but instead about 10am, was very hot. We'll worth the slog to the top although quite busy, take water with you. The views are fab right down the Ella gap.
title: Beautiful views

body: We've been there at sunset and the place is really nice, overcrowded though. The hike is pretty easy, it takes around 30-40 min to get to the top. Even if it's full of tourists, I liked that you can easily find a little spot for yourself to admire the beauty of the lush green hills all around. If you are in Ella, you should probably see it.
title: Stunning views of Ella's hills

body: Arrived by car at 5:20 and walked using mobile phone light. First part was very easy and steady, the last few minutes were steeper but, by then, it was light enough not to be a problem. There were a lovely range of hues as the minutes passed. Plenty of time to move around (there are a few spots to choose from at the top), take heaps of photos and enjoy sunrise.
title: Worth the early wake up call

body: First of all you do not need to take a tuktuk. You can easily walk in 45 minutes from the city to the peak. The view is nice and even when it is clowdy the sunset is worth the hike
title: Great view and beautiful sunset.

body: A moderate hike to first peak with lots of steps. The path to second peak is quiet challenging. Stunning view!
title: Stunning view

body: Hearing nature waking up is amazing while seeing the sunrise. The hike is pretty easy would recommend to take a flashlight with you .Really worth getting up and being there for 5.30am
title: Worth it for sunrise

body: Enjoyable walk and only got difficult when you started climbing the stairs. The views are very good and there are plenty of photo opportunities. Plenty of locals also selling water, fruit etc all the way and including the top.
title: Worth the walk up here

body: Joyful place to enjoy with friends when climbing up on the mountain and you can see the awesome view of ella from here
title: Little Adam's peak

body: Quite challenging to climb, takes about 20 minutes to reach the top, but the view is very nice. Ella rock looks majestic from there.
title: Very nice view point

body: Was a nice small hike with an amazing view worth the hike and can enjoy the Zipline as well , forgien adults for the Zipline cost about LKR 4500

body: Great little hike. Only took about 25 mins to get up. We did it in the middle of the day and the heat was fine. Plenty of kids doing it when we did it. Would recommend doing it the day prior to doing Ella Rock as you can be quite sore after Ella Rock haha

body: Climb up the little Adam's peak is kind of obligatory while staying in ella. Recomend to go till the last of the four hills though it is hard under the sun. Great panorama!
title: Spectacular view

body: It took us only an hour to finish this trek. The view was amazing. We started next to flower garden and enjoyed King coconuts on the way. The weather was nice which elevated our experience.
title: A must do easy trek

body: It is an amazing experience to climb to the top of the peak. When you are there there is so much blue so much green. You need to take a moment and just enjoy the view. p.s. there are friendly dogs too....
title: So much blue

body: Great 30-minutes outdoor adventure for all the family members, see the pictures and you will understand. From Ella head to 98 Acres and once there just follow the signs. Expect steep steps. Anyone can hike it. It's only a half an hour!You will see Ella Rock!
title: Great outdoor adventure

Otherwise this is a must do in Ella.

body: Great walk and great views. About 1 hour to walk up. Quite a few steps and a bit of rocky Hill to climb.

title: Wear a hat!

body: We had gone to ella from nuwara just for a day trip. Our first stop was Little adams peak. Entry is free for everyone. A beautiful half hour hike leads u to awe inspiring views from the top. Its a very easy climb. Wear comfortable shoes. Carry water. Almost near d summit, there are activities available. Like flying ravana,a zipline adventure. Quad bike etc. If u r in ella, dont miss climbing d Little Adams Peak. Can see Ella Rock,Ravana Falls from here.
title: Easy hike

body: It took 1,5 hours up and down. It wasn't so cold for European - shorts and shirt were fine. Views are awesome! There was other hill, we didn't go there (so, 1,5 hours was enough for us).
title: Great viewpoints

body: Myself, my husband and my parents (who are mid 70s) did this walk and although it isn’t hard it isn’t as easy as I had read either! The first half of the walk is lovely - on a gently sloping path with wonderful views. The 2nd part of the walk was a bit more difficult with about 300 steps up to the top - it is fine if you pace yourself and take regular stops although I did find it hard going on my knees on the way down! The view is definitely worth it though, you get an amazing view of Ella Rock on the way up, and a 360 degree view once you are at the top. On a good day I am told you can see as far as the Sea but it was a bit hazy the day we were there but you still had amazing views.I would definitely recommend going up - just pace yourself!
title: Worth the hike to the top

body: You'll have a smile of accomplishment when you reach the top and gaze at the beautiful scenery. I am a big guy (150kg) so the trek up was not easy, but there are plenty of small areas to rest and catch your breath. Though all uphill, there was no part that seemed too steep or particularly difficult. The views are breathtaking and you really feel alone in the world for split second.

body: We were lucky to have a beautiful weather. I highly recommend the early wake-up. Bring a jacket as he could be freezing @ this time

body: By the standards of other climbs in Sri Lanka, the trek to the top is more than manageable and the views when you get there are well worth the effort. Make sure you get some freshly squeezed lime juice while you're up there too from the nice young man at the top. Highly recommended.
title: Amazing views

body: Lovely views of Ella Rock and surrounding mountains. Took about 30 - 45 minutes to get to the top and the views were well worth it. Lots of coconut sellers along the way.

body: A fairly easy walk that starts about 10 minutes walk out from Ella (very close to the path out to Nine Arch Bridge). If you want, you can take a tuktuk part of the way but it's not a tough climb. You can get a drink (and even a foot massage) halfway up. The last section is steep with lots of steps and a little bit of scrambling over steeper sections. The views over Ella Rock are well worth the climb!
title: Easy climb and great views

body: Trailing through the picturesque premises of 98 Acres Resort is the Little Adams Peak. From the top one could get a 360 degrees view of the whole terrific mountain terrain surrounding the Ella valley. Entry to the premises is free of charge. There is a plenty of recreational activities such as Flying Fox, Air rifling, archery and ACT and so on. All are being operated at high standards yet very reasonable rates by the resort itself. Non-alcoholic drinks are also available at the kiosk located halfway the beautiful hike.
title: One of the most scenic spots in Ella

body: It doesn't take very long but is a fairly steep climb towards the end if you wanna get all the way to little adams peak. However, first peak you reach is pretty easy to get to and views are just as stunning. Can hike directly from Ella. Totally worth a visit.
title: Beautiful views

body: Starts about 10 min walk outside Ella. Quite an easy hike with a couple of scrambly bits but most hard surface or steps. You can get drinks halfway up/ down and the view from the top is quite good - morning better as it was beginning to cloud over as we came down. Don’t expect peace and solitude as this is very popular. We’re into birdwatching and there we lots to see.
title: Nice little hike

body: Climbing the peak is not really hard. The views are breathtaking. A must ser being on Ella. There is also a zip line for 2000rps per person.
title: Impressive view

body: Little Adams Peak is a must do in Ella. The walk is fairly easy and the rewards are great. You have outstanding views of Ella! I would definitely recommend this hike.
title: A Great Hike in Ella

body: The hike to the summit is a short one (especially if you take a tuktuk to the beginning of the scenic walk) but the end part can be quite challenging due to steep slopes and even terrain. title: Great views, short hike

body: This has better views than Hortons plains and only takes 30 mins to get up to the top Just wear sensible shoes
title: Nice views

body: Beautiful and relatively easy walk although is quite hilly at the end, so try to do it when is not too hot. Less than five minutes away from where the walk starts you can find the path to the Nine Arches Bridge.
title: Hiking

body: we start the hike around 5.30 and it was an easy way up ( we traveled with a 2 year old toddler ) you can get a three-wheeler for the first 200 mtrs. they will charge you around 300 LKRJust before the hike starts at the very beginning there is a cafe and bar offering very good food and also a clean toilet facility for 50 LKR.Once you reach the top there are three peeks . one with Buddha statue and two more . you can reach two with kids but not the third. title: MUST DO ATTRACTION ...!!!! Amazing

body: Amazing view of the sun rising over the ridge. We went up at 5.30am and was at the top just after 6.10am watch the sun rise at 6.30am. Not too bad a walk and mostly on steps however wear enclosed trainers. Free to do and some great views from the top. Get up early to enjoy this place.
title: Adams Peak Sunrise

body: Went here with GF around 10 o'clock, which was a time we were very happy with. Nice views. No scammers. Joyfull!
title: Dawn trip

body: Trek up the Little Adam’s Peak, EllaOne of the prettiest spots and most popular treks in Ella is up the Little Adam’s Peak. However, we came across an unexpected hazard. When we reached the point where the zipline takes off, we saw a sign posted which said, “drone cameras can trigger a bee attack.” There were no drone cameras evident, but very soon there was a bee attack. While we escaped, my driver waiting below said that about 20 people had to be taken to the hospital. I believe the authorities need to take care of this. If there are bees in the vicinity of this very popular spot and inclined to attack visitors, something must be done as a whole vacation can get ruined if one gets caught in a bee attack. Till this is sorted out, the literature should also give some guidelines for persons on how to avoid the bee attack and how to respond in case of one. One important thing I learnt by going through Google/Bing is that you never swat or try to fend off the bees but run as fast as you can and look for shelter. In spite of the beautiful trek, the rating reflects the hazard which the tourists were subjected to.
title: Bee attack - Need to be careful

body: Great hike. Perfect for a day tour of Ella and surrounding sites. Don't know why this site requires 100 characters to describe something this simple.
title: Quick hike

body: Paved most of the way and gentle to start with steps and then very steep stairs for last part, but very much worth the trek for the views. Many vendors selling water and coconuts along the way.
title: Must Do

body: Little Adam's Peak is an awesome little mountain to hike at, which includes a fair bit of rock scrambling. It gives amazing views of Ella from the top so this hike is definitely worth taking!
title: Awesome hike

body: It's free to ascend to the peak. It takes about an hour, with short stops on the way to get your breath back! It's a little rough in places so wear sturdy trainers. It's worth it when you get to the top as there is a Buddha and a 360 degree view of the surrounding magnificent countryside and hills. You can do the zip line here for a charge. It's well worth the climb if you're in the area. Tip - do in the early morning or late afternoon when it's less hot.
title: Stunning Views at the Top!

body: Lovely views and a must to do, the hills of Sri lanka are beautiful, it was great weather when we were there , not sure if it would work on a rainy day
title: Lovely views

body: STUNNING VIEW MUST DO. pretty easy walk , all up hill some stairs but would recommend wearing enclosed shoes.
title: A MUST

body: Nice easy walk to the peak rewarded with spectacular views. The walk is not difficult and only took us about 20 minutes. If you are in the area I would highly recommend taking the time to do this activity. They also have a great zip line and abseiling half way up for those that want a quick way down.
title: Worth the walk

body: Loved Little Adams Peak! For those more seasoned hikers, it’s a very easy walk up with a mixtures is steps and path but it’s definitely manageable for anyone :)There are people selling drinks, snacks & souvenirs on the way - we bought a magnet from one of the ladies and had a lovely chat about her life (which was sad but she never lost her smile!) - so nice to support the locals.There are two peaks: once you have reached the first peak, you can continue on the path which descends before ascending again. This path is more challenging and you have to scramble a bit. Wear trainers! We chose to do the Ravine Zipline on our way down which was amazing and so worth it!
title: Good things come in “little” packages...

body: Don't miss out on this amazing walk it is so much worth the effort. If you like keep exploring the other peaks around.
title: Well worth the effort

body: This little mountain is situated in just like 3 km away from Ella town. You have to walk through a tea estate for about 1 km from the nearest car park. But it is worthwhile. Climb takes about 15 minutes one way. From top you can see Ella rock, Ravana waterfalls, 98 acres hotel and Mahamewna Pagoda as well.Along the way you meet Flying Ravana Team as well. So if you are up for a zipline ride and be adventurous that is a plus point.

body: The route is easy to walk. We started the walk at 5:30am to see the sunrise. We were on the top right on time (took only l20mins or so to walk up there) and got to see the beautiful sunrise. Suggest this location because of the easy walk (you can even get a tuktuk almost to the top) and beautiful mountain landscape.

body: Not over strenuous but you do need some appropriate footware. Its not flip flop territory. body: 741146582Very good view from the top with tea farms and mountains. Lots of nice photo spots. Definitely worth the trip

body: Nice and quite easy path to get to the top of the mountain. Worth walking for beautiful views and calming sourroundings.

body: It is a nice hour and half hike, nature is just beautiful and you will enjoy the view at the top too..

body: The most favorite place I have visited. The view s amazing, the Bit wind blowing some times, It’s wonderful experience that I have. I love this place a lot , I request to everyone to visit to Ella & climb mini Adams peak.

body: Went here for a nice walk after being stuck in a car for several hours. Living in the Peaks we walk a lot. We could see a path which seemed to wind around the mountain. Good views but nothing we couldn’t see from our hotel.

body: The walk up to Little Adam’s Peak is doable by most people although those with mobility issues might give this one a pass. Easy flat first bit through tea plantation fields up to the zip line company office (where there are very clean toilets). Then the track gets more difficult and some scrambling is required. Over 300 steps/stairs and then the scrambling up to the top. However, the view is well worth the hike and the exercise is great for the legs and lungs. Once at the top you can go further but it is more difficult with a path that requires good strength and endurance. Total time to go up would be about an hour depending on your level of fitness. A must do!
title: Little Adam’s Peak - a must do event in Ella!

body: The beginning of the walk is very gentle but after the zip line point it does become more challenging. Views from the top are breathtaking. The option of having a foot massage before heading back down is brilliant and does soothe tired legs. Be aware that the zip line is only for a very short run and that you cannot take a bag. You store you bag in a locker and then after taking the zip line climb back up to retrieve your bag.
title: Long trek for a great view

body: A nice hike with lovely views at every turn.Don’t believe the signs, it is considerably longer than the 500 m noted at the entry point. (In fact, a second sign more than 1/2 km in read 650 m further...)Regardless, it is more than worth it!There are local vendors along the path selling water, cold drinks, King coconut and other offerings.The Mega Zipline is accessible just before the summit climb. There are cools pots to sit and rest, if you wish.
title: Lovely views

body: True enough that its a breathtaking view from the top of the Little Adams Peak at Ella but if you are a serious trekker challenge your self to do the real thing - the 5,500 step + tracking stretches of the Historical ADAMS PEAK that will take approx 3 - 4 hours from the base from one of the more popular access routes (Hatton - Nallathanniya / 4 hours away from Ella)Not only is it a thrilling experience with spectacular views along the way, the highlight is the sunrise from the eastern skies once you are at the peak which is absolutely breathtaking. For Sri Lankans Sri Pada assumes huge historic and religious importance and if you eventually decide to do it you will be treading along a path that was negotiated many centuries ago by historic travelers in the caliber of Buddhist traveler Fa Hien (411–12 CE) , Italian merchant / seafarer Marco Polo (1298 CE), Arab traveler Ibn Battuta (1344 CE) and in more recent history by John Davy, brother of the Sir Humphry Davy (1817 CE)The climbing season is considered to be from December to May. Off-season climbing is possible but considered more challenging and possibly best suited for seasoned trekkers. Best time of the day to climb the mountain will be starting from night, targeting to reach the top by early morning to view the sunriseMy first experience in scaling Adams Peak was in 1988 at a teenager and i have repeated the feat couple of times there after close to those times. I have been trying to convince my family to do it a group since of late and is still to succeed.
title: A sneak preview of the real thing - The 5500 step + tracking stretch of the real ADAMS PEAK

body: Lovely view from the top. We set off at 5am which was lucky as we went the wrong way. There are signs but there was a closed gate so we took a path down into a tea plantation which finally lead to a dead end. Had to double back and walk around the closed gate. Still made it up before sunrise at 5:55am. Obviously that will change with the time of year.
title: Sunrise hike on Jan 17 2020

body: My wife and I enjoyed a great hike here and really enjoyed the spectacular views of Ella rock and the surrounding landscape. I would say it took us about an hour total from the very bottom. I would definitely recommend this if you enjoy hiking, its not too strenuous and definitely worth the time.
title: Great Hike, breathtaking views

body: Keep walking up the road and locals will guide you to Little Adam's Peak. Easy to find. Have lunch in one of many cafes along the way, ecellent food.
title: Good place to take photos of mountains.

body: Google maps put it miles away so from town we got a tuk tuk who basically took us to our accommodation and said walk ( it's an easy walk from town). It's an easy walk, all the way up, the views get better and better as you go up and were amazing from the top. There are various activities to do up there like ziplining, atvs, abseiling, we gave that stuff a miss having done it other places but all looked pretty well set up and we'll organised.
title: Really easy climb and awesome views

body: A nice walk among the tea plantation to reach the top. A short set of stairs to the top. When it's busy it would be difficult to get up and down without waiting
title: Worth the trip

body: Little Adam's Peak is a very beautiful place to watch. It is located in the hilly region of Srilanka.
title: Little Adam's Peak

body: It begins in quite an easy incline and there are lots of families with young kids enjoying the walk. Once you reach the top though there are three other peaks which you can walk to and the second of them is quite the challenge. Some amazing opportunities for photos and for meeting people from other countries. My wife and I offered to take a photo for a couple of different people and now we are Instagram friends 😄
title: Well worth the trek...

body: Really nice walk and not to long. Really great views of Ella when you get to the top.Just make sure to wear walking boots or shoes. Probably can get away with trainers with good grip. A lot of people trying to get up their with flip flops / sandals on which is not the brightest idea and can’t imagine very comfortable.You can also do a zip wire down if you want also which you will see on the walk up. Not sure on the price as we did not do it, but looked fun.
title: Nice walk and great views

body: If you are not a big fan of hours spending on hike, try Little Adam’s Peak which takes approximately an hour or so up and down. Adam’s Peak takes 6-7 hours to climb and our guide told us it can get crowded too especially during full moon as locals go up to pray. On top of Little Adam’s Peak gives one a great view of Ella and a close look of Ella Rock, another place for hike adventurist as heard there’s no proper trail on Ella Rock. Little Adam’s Peak’s trails are mainly steps and up to 3/4 of the way, one can also try the zip line. Great view and recommended for non hikers.
title: Easy hike to get a view

body: For the first 500m you can take a tuk for like 300 rupees (or a 5 minute quick walk) and then there's a foot path of roughly 700m leading to the flying ravana base. From there onwards there are steps leading to the little adams peak which would take a rough 15-20 mins to climb for a young adult. Great view! and an easy hike
title: Good for a hike with kids

body: Great walk, even in thongs!! Went to the other peak as well. Well worth it !! Easy walk from the town centre or via tuk tuk or your own scooter like we had.
title: Awesome

body: Magnificent 360 degree views from the top. Views Across the team plantations and mountains and a small golden Buddha at the top make it a very tranquil location. We are not the fittest couple so took our time and found the climb doable. Best was early in the morning and experience that morning sun.
title: Worth the walk

body: Beautiful trek leading to mesmerising views, calm breezes and some adventures on the go. Moderate trek, carry some water along and be a bit careful on the top, somewhere very steep climb, overall doable - we did with little children along.On the way you will find tea plantations., Ravana Ziplines, Mountain Biking, ATV bike riding experience - Everything is chargeable, choose your thrill !

body: Little Adam’s peak doesn’t disappoint you. To the first peak, the hiking was quite moderate. But if you still have some energy left, you should go to two other peaks after the first one. It’s just a little bit more hard hike than the first peak, but the view is amazing and much less people around you. You feel great after teaching all the points! You can feel the nature and meditate or relax as you go up!

body: So we attempted to follow google to the base of little Adams Peak which took us completely off track and we needed up in the middle of a local village within the forest. Quite scary for 3 women! The locals constantly wanted to charge us for their help. In the end a local told us the correct way out and we managed to find the correct path, which was nearly at the summit. We ascended the peak through tea plantations which clearly wasn’t the right way. The main entrance to the site is just at the end of the main road from the town centre of Ella. Follow the tourists and not google. That being said it’s totally worth the climb. The views are amazing. A must do in Ella.
title: Don’t follow google

body: We started at 98 Acres and walked the easy pathway towards Little Adam's Peak. teapickers were dotted about the plantation and the views of Ella Rock were spectacular. We had two little ones so weren't fussed about reaching the top. We enjoyed the walk for approx an hour there and back.

body: I thought it would be a far more difficult walk up but this is an easy walk with some steps. Don’t be intimidated if you are not fit - you will be able to do it and the views are worth it. If you are going to Ella you should include this.

body: Short walk that ends up with stunning view. And thats it. It was nit crowded arround 9. I think everybody goes there at 7 to see the sunrise

body: Really easy to follow hike walk up to the top.Lovely views all around and fun walking to all 3 peaks.

body: We've just got back from a holiday in Sri Lanka that, both myself and my wife agree, is the best holiday we have ever had. We were meet at the airport by Rohan from Danulanka Tours, who would be our driver, photographer and tour guide for the next two weeks.The advantage of a local driver is not to be underestimated – as is the case in India, driving follows a set of rules that have no discernible pattern to drivers from other countries. Tolerances are measured in millimetres and cat-like reflexes are required that have been honed over many years.Rohan had an earlier career working as a photographer, which meant he was more than happy to take photographs at the various places we visited over the two weeks – a definite improvement over the clichéd selfie.Official tour guides in Sri Lanka are strictly controlled – you can be sure that any official guide will have a good knowledge of the history of any historical site in Sri Lanka. The additional benefits of a tour guide is they know when you need to arrive to get the most out your visit – whether that is to catch the ceremony at The Temple of the Tooth, or when you need to leave to get the view at World’s End, before it is obscured by cloud (5am btw, so we did a walk to Little Adam’s Peak instead).Although we had agreed a pre-defined itinerary, Rohan was more than happy to make adjustments along the way and to take into account any specific interests we had.When we commented how much better the fruit tasted in Sri Lanka than the UK, Rohan went out his way to stop en-route to pick up whatever was local to the area through which we were travelling.For example:Yellow bananas – smaller that those in the UK, but ten times more delicious.Red bananas – even nicer than yellow bananas.Mangos – several different varieties. The big ones are particularly nice, and are enough for two.Yellow coconuts – lots of milk, and then split to eat the thin white layer. Much nicer than green…Jack fruits – never heard of these before. Had the strangest consistency and taste, but definitely recommended.A drink made from a fruit that only grows in mud flats in one area of Sri Lanka – can’t remember what it was called, but it is a must try.Cashew nuts – also sold by the side of the road. Almost creamy in flavour.Rohan proved invaluable in other ways as well: on our Jeep safari through Yala National Park, he spotted a Leopard in a tree - something no-one else in the vehicle (including the driver) had spotted. We had several minutes watching the Leopard, before it decided to climb down – as the most anyone else saw that day was a tail disappearing into the scrub, I am grateful for Rohan’s keen eyesight.Sadly, since the bombing earlier this year, tourists numbers are down 80% - this means Sri Lanka is currently a real bargain. You can stay in 4 and 5 star hotels, for the price of 2 or 3 star.Finally, I will say Sri Lanka is a must visit - the people are happy and friendly, and it is clean (I think even less litter that the UK). The wildlife is plentiful, even outside the wildlife parks - this is probably helped by the predominantly Buddhist culture, and the fact that farmers are compensated for any damage done by elephants.Give Sri Lanka and Danulanka Tours a go – you will not be disappointed.
title: Tour of Sri Lanka, including Little Adam's Peak

body: A wanderful spot at Ella. Hiking at an easy to medium level, incredible view and tasty coconut and guava juice on the way up.

body: Got up to watch the sunrise from little Adam's peak, the sunrise wasn't the best as it was cloudy but the views were beautiful. It was a super easy walk and well sign posted! Worth doing it in the morning because it's not too hot

body: I was not quite fit enough to make it to all 4 peaks but did do 2. Stunning views. Take lots of water and try to go before it gets too hot
title: Beautiful place

body: Good walk through the town and up to the Peak. Quite a few steps at the end so all pretty straightforward. Really impressive views from the top. Highly recommended.
title: Nice little walk

body: Nice walk from the hotel. first half an hour on the train rails until the nine arches bridge and then a shortcut to Little Adams peak. we stayed at the mountain heavens hotel

body: We were a little concerned about whether or not we would enjoy this as neoth myself or my wife are particularly active or in to hiking but decided to give it a go. I think the walk to the top took about an hour and a half from Ella, we did stop for photos quite a bit. The views all the way up are beautiful and walking through the Tea plantation with the ladies picking the tea leaves was a great experience.We did have to stop to catch our breath a few times but it was absolutely worth it. If we return to Ella we will take the walk again and also recommend to anyone.We took the B113 to the 98 Acres Resort, followed the signs (the are big as the zip line company have massive signs) then on the way back down followed the slightly different route to the 9 arch bridge then walked the railway tracks back in to Ella.... Definately the way to do it in my opinion!!Don't miss it!!!

body: The hike up alot of stairs was definitely worth the effort for the stunning panoramic views.I have read reviews that say it's an easy walk but I don't necessarily agree with that.All the same it was definitely worth the effort.We decided on the spur of the moment to ride the zip line.What a great professional outfit. The ridge climbs are much more difficult but still fun and gets you away from the majority of other tourists. I'd recommend walking boots or good solid footwear. Also if you can, try to go mid week as it can be pretty busy at the weekends. All in all though, a great few hours and a must if you're in Ella.

Probably the best view of Ella rock and you can also see Ravana fallsWhat we didn’t like:- very busy. Since it’s so easy to get to and there is a zip-line entrance along the way it can distract from the natural beauty of the place.What to consider:- go early or go late. body: #Little #Adams #Peak #Hiking Ella is a hiking hotspot in the mountain country of Sri Lanka. Some of the views from hikes in Ella are phenomenal with the region well known for its tea plantations and spectacular mountain ranges. If you want to enjoy some of the best views without needing to hike for hours, Little Adam’s Peak is the perfect trek, especially for an unforgettable sunset. It’s one of the top things to do in Sri Lanka if you enjoy hiking!The trail begins with a moderate incline as it winds through tea plantations. It will lead you up to 1141m above sea-level although you already begin at a high elevation so you will only hike up a few hundred meters. The trail is marked the whole way with well-maintained paths and stairs to the first set of viewpoints. There are multiple platforms, rocks, and viewpoints perfect for photos once you hit the top of Little Adam’s Peak. Although, you can and should keep going along the ridge and the view only gets better.As you continue along the ridge the trail gets a little wilder and you might get a little dirty, managing your way up and down to the final viewpoint.We hung out at the top of Little Adam’s Peak with no one else around, taking in the mountains and the epic scenery of the 360-degree views. We probably waited a little too long to head back and ended up trekking back down in the dark. For just a short hike, Little Adam’s Peak gives you unbelievable views and is the ideal way to spend sunset in Ella. body: Climbing Little Adams peak was one of the activities our tour guide had organised for us whilst in Ella. Setting off early in the morning to avoid the heat we assume, it is a fairly steady walk along for a while, then a climb up some steps to the top. You do not need to be an Olympic athlete to climb this, but a certain level of fitness is required, and the last bit is quite steep; those used to walking and hiking should find it a breeze. The whole climb up and back took approx. 2 hours, but you will definitely work up a sweat doing so ! I would strongly recommend sensible footwear e.g. trainers or walking shoes, and some water !On the way up we passed some tea pickers in the fields next to the path, who were more than happy to pose for some pictures, for a small reward / LKR tip of course !Once at the top there is another good photo opportunity stood next to the small statue / shrine, and then some absolutely stunning views over the surrounding countryside and the valley below. There is a large rock ledge where everyone takes their turn to stand on or dangle their legs over the edge and take photos.On the way back down we passed the tea pickers again, who were now having some food - probably lunch since they start so early in the morning ? There was also a little coconut / drinks shack hut that had opened up on the way down, where you can buy a well deserved cold drink to cool down with.A very enjoyable way to see more of the great beauty of Sri Lanka.
title: Fairly easy hike with amazing views, a must do if visiting Ella !

body: This is a short hike that isn’t challenging. It doesn’t take long, but provides incredible views. It gets hot, so take water from the main town before you go. Sometimes there’s a man selling ice cold water - literally a massive chunk of ice in the bottle - close to the top for 120 LKR. If you see him, buy the water. It’s the coldest and most satisfying water you’ll get in Sri Lanka!!

body: Little Adam’s Peak is a fairly easy hike found in Ella, Sri Lanka and is a short 20-minute walk from the center of town. Also, it’s completely FREE! The entrance is easily located on Google maps, but just in case, you can find the entrance between The Chillout Ella and the Ella Flower Garden Resort. The hike starts with a very slow ascent through a dirt path surrounded by tea fields and stunning views of the lush green valleys that shroud hill country. You’ll make your way along said path for about 15-minutes depending on your walking speed where you’ll see the staircase that leads all the way to the peak; you literally cannot miss it! The best time to climb Little Adam’s Peak would be sunrise. There aren’t many early risers, therefore you will beat the crowds if you go for sunrise. Little Adam’s Peak has a great effort to view ratio which is why tourists flock here all year round to catch glimpses of the beautiful tea country laid out below.
title: Easy hike with stunning views

We entered beyond the turn off for Nine Arch Bridge which means less of a climb up as you’re starting higher up. We then left via the other exit which brought us out closer to Ella. As well as the main Peak you can also continue further down a steep slope (with steps sort of cut into the clay bank) and up another slope to a second peak. Both peaks give excellent views of the area. If you are going to go to the second Peak it’s worthwhile taking shoes, not jandals or flip flops.

body: Not sure why this is called "Little Adam's Peak", as it has nothing in common with Adam' Peak (Sri Pada). Firstly, "Little Adam's Peak" is a hike through nature, on dirt paths, beautiful scenery, tea plantations, mountain peaks. Secondly, the view is incredible ! Unfortunately, many people skip this place due to the name confusion, since the name suggests this is something similar but less nice than Adam's Peak. Again, there is no similarity between the two. This place has stunning views and it's in the heart of nature. We went there on two consecutive days (the first day we were late and the sun was already setting). body: Among the attractions in Sri Lanka, Little Adam's Peak impressed me most with her natural rustic setting, breathtaking mountainous scenery and memorable hike. I was born and brought up in a metropolis city bombarded with irritating noise from the zooming vehicles and factory machineries; the atmosphere pervaded with toxic pollutants from the car exhausts and industrial chimneys. But here in Ella and the Little Adam's Peak, the setting was so different with lush greenery everywhere and very far from the madding crowd. As I slowly wandered among the lush greenery, the lyrics of the Happy Wanderer resonates in my ear:I like to go a wandering up the mountain track. And as I go, I love to singMy knapsack on my back. Val-deri, val-dera. Val-deri, val-deraHa, ha, ha, ha, ha, ha Ha Val-dera. My knapsack on my backAnother thing wonderful about Ella is that the nearby attractions, be it this Little Adam's Peak, the Nine Arch Bridge, the waterfall are all within walking distance from the train station and near the town center. The hike to Little Adam's Peak was comfortably done without I even realized that I was at the summit of the mountain. It was something slightly more difficult than climbing Bukit Timah Hill in Singapore. Early morning at about 6.30 am, I strolled my way from my hostel to the town center. The road to the Little Adam's Peak is on the left turn from the town center. I had my simple breakfast of a plate of two pieces of coconut roti with a cup of Ceylonese tea in one of the restaurants along the road to the scenic attraction. There was a morning bazaar on the street just at the junction of the town center and the adjoining road to the Little Adam's Peak. I enjoyed seeing the locals in their daily morning routine. It took me about half an hour to arrive at the base of the Little Adam's Peak. The lush greenery of the tea plantations that followed and the rustic setting of the village and the hillside track really uplifted my hiking spirit. The magnificent looming Ella Rock mountain appeared robustly gorgeous and was a beautiful sight as we hike up the track to the summit. It was a uphill laborious climb though it was not that high. I was panting heavily as the steps were steep but the moment I reached the summit, the panoramic mountainous view was spectacularly impressive and gorgeous. Breathtaking views and a rustic scenery. The air is fresh, the environment calm and peaceful and the scenery beautiful. It is waste if you miss this when you are in Ella.
title: Rustic, breathtaking and memorable

body: The other reviews talk about the stairs, zip line, etc.The walk up is not difficult, there are beautiful breezes, views, scenery. It’s lovely and we recommend going.At the top of the first peak you come to (the ice cream man is likely there), there are some stray dogs that definitely depend on tourists to survive. We brought a large tin bowl and filled it with water. We also brought a lot of dry dog food. Please bring something for these precious, sweet dogs when you go. You can refill the bowl with water and bring food.Also, the ice cream that the man there is selling is really good. A lot of people were buying ice cream cones (he filled each cone with vanilla ice cream). We had a cone each. Parents were buying for kids and themselves. We also bought two cones for the dog that apparently had puppies. (Not sure where the puppies were. Hopefully someone rescued them.) We held the cones while she licked the ice cream. So, Little Adam’s Peak, including the walk through town to get there, is so nice and we recommend it. But please remember to think of the dogs and help them. 🧡
